label: 2026 Orbital Launches
delta: As of Aug 11-12: 96+ Falcon-family launches in 2026 — two Starlink missions flew Aug 11: Starlink 10-19 (SLC-40 Cape Canaveral, B1085 18th flight, delayed a day by a scrub) and Starlink 17-49 (SLC-4E Vandenberg, B1103 5th flight, 73rd Starlink mission from Vandenberg), part of a rare 3-launches-in-7-days West Coast stretch. SpaceX passed its 90th Falcon 9 launch of the year on Aug 4 and its 50th launch from the West Coast in 2026 on Aug 8. President Gwynne Shotwell projects ~140-145 Falcon 9 launches for the full year. Previously: 600th flight-proven-booster launch, Starlink 10-45 (July 14, SLC-40 Cape Canaveral, B1080 28th flight, 638th booster recovery overall); record 36th single-booster reflight, Starlink 10-42 (July 9, B1067, SLC-40). Also in this window: Starship IFT-13 flew (test flight, not counted toward this Falcon-family total) — T-0 abort July 16, successful launch July 24.

label: Total Booster Recoveries (All-Time)
delta: 649th: OCISLY landing after the Aug 11 Starlink 17-49 mission from Vandenberg (B1103, 5th flight). 648th: ASOG landing after the Aug 11 Starlink 10-19 mission from Cape Canaveral (B1085, 18th flight). 647th: booster landing during the Aug 8 Starlink West Coast mission (163rd touchdown on droneship A Shortfall of Gravitas). 638th: ASOG landing (Starlink 10-45, July 14, SLC-40 Cape Canaveral — B1080 28th flight; SpaceX's 600th flight-proven-booster launch overall; ASOG's 161st touchdown). 635th: ASOG landing (Starlink 10-42, July 9, SLC-40 — B1067's record 36th flight; ASOG's 160th touchdown). Note: IFT-12 Booster 19 (May 22) and IFT-13 Booster 20 (July 24) were NOT recovered — both lost during off-nominal landing-burn/splashdown attempts in Gulf of Mexico ocean landings (Starship boosters are not counted in this Falcon-family recovery tally).

label: Starlink Satellites in Orbit
delta: 10,898 satellites in orbit (10,882 operational) as of early Aug 2026, out of 12,644 ever launched (per KeepTrack X-Report). SpaceX filed an FCC application July 6 for up to 100,000 Gen3 satellites across two new VLEO shells with W-/D-band frequencies, positioned as AI-data-center backhaul infrastructure in addition to consumer broadband. S-1 confirmed 10.3M subscribers (doubled YoY); ARPU $66/month (Q1 2026). Aug 4 Q2 earnings: Starlink drove the majority of SpaceX's $7.81B quarterly revenue.

label: Starlink Subscribers
delta: 10.3M subscribers confirmed in S-1 filing (doubled YoY). Starlink segment profit: $1.2B in most recent quarter. 160+ countries served. ARPU: $66/month Q1 2026.

label: Max Single Booster Reflights
delta: B1067 set a new record with its 36th flight on the Starlink 10-42 mission (July 9, 2026, SLC-40 Cape Canaveral) — the first orbital booster in history to reach 36 flights. Previously: 34th flight on Starlink 10-44 (Mar 30, 2026).

label: Starship Integrated Flight Tests
delta: IFT-13 (Booster 20 V3 + Ship 40 V3) completed July 24, 2026 after a July 16 T-0 abort (6 Raptors flagged low LOX turbopump pressure from moisture; 2 engines replaced before reflight). Results: first-ever deployment of operational satellites — 20 V3 Starlink sats (6 with cameras) released in suborbit and contacted ground stations; Ship 40 relit all 3 Raptors and made a soft Indian Ocean splashdown, remaining intact afterward for the first close-up post-flight heat-shield inspection. Booster 20 was lost on its Gulf of Mexico splashdown attempt — only 10 of 13 landing-burn engines relit, 5 shut down seconds later, causing a hard impact. IFT-14 (Booster 21 + Ship 41) is in static-fire testing at Starbase; Musk has floated a late-August window (FAA-dependent), targeting the first delivery of operational V3 Starlinks to full orbit and a possible first tower catch attempt of the upper stage. Prior: FAA cleared Starship to resume flights July 13, 2026, closing the IFT-12 mishap investigation (heat effects on propulsion + erroneous engine alarm settings that prevented Booster 19's reignition, May 22 loss).

label: SPCX (Nasdaq) — Post-IPO Trading
source: SEC EDGAR S-1 / CNBC / Bloomberg / Nasdaq
contestNote: Trading around $146.15/share intraday Aug 13, 2026 (up 9.65%, extending a four-day rally of 40%+; 52-week range $104.83–$225.64). SPCX fell below its $135 IPO price for the first time July 15 and bottomed near $104.83 on Aug 3. Since then: Aug 6 lock-up expiration released up to 911.5M insider shares (~$100B) without triggering a sell-off (+6.1%); shares jumped 15.8% Aug 7-8 on the Q2 earnings beat, the $16.8B Terafab chip-plant confirmation, and the pending $60B Cursor (Anysphere) deal; reclaimed the $135 IPO price Aug 10 (+4%); surged 9.6% Aug 12 after Musk said AI/Grok revenue could overtake Starlink and launch revenue within 1-2 months; and rose a further 9.65% Aug 13 after a filing showed Musk's 48.4% stake is worth over $900B, even as a second, ~$42.5B share unlock (~320M shares) looms Aug 20. IPO recap: priced at $135/share June 11 (largest IPO in history, $1.77T implied valuation); all-time high $225.64 June 16; joined Nasdaq-100 July 7. Musk holds ~42-48% economic equity (filings vary by measurement date), ~79-85% voting control (dual-class Class B) — cannot be removed as director except by his own vote.
